title: The Iran War and the Midterms | The President’s Inbox
summary: Council on Foreign Relations podcast before the November 2026 US midterms on the stalled US-Iran war and whether Trump will escalate after the vote.

assertions.quote: the United States finds itself in a stalemate with Iran, with each side waiting for the other to blink.

verdicts.note: Two former NSC Iran directors and the host describe a stalemate in October 2026; this is not independently verified here.
By April 2026 the war had reached political deadlock, both sides claimed victory and the ceasefire came with no agreement on any US or Iranian point, but it ended in a truce rather than a static war.

assertions.quote: The war has spiked the prices of gas and diesel
They're not necessarily going to go to war for Iran, but they're more than happy to let them be a thorn in our side.
We took out a large swath of the Iranian leadership, including the supreme leader. But that didn't solve the problem.

verdicts.note: The war was launched on the bet that killing Iran's leadership would trigger an uprising and collapse; instead a younger, more hardline leadership took over, though the paper does not credit decentralised command.

assertions.quote: they're not cracking. You know, we're not seeing any elite or security defections.

verdicts.note: Analysts report no significant defections through 2026, though this is hard to verify from outside.

assertions.quote: they like doubled and ultimately like tripled their imports of Iranian oil.

verdicts.note: Tanker-tracking estimates put China's share of Iran's exported oil at around 90 percent, bought through intermediaries.
US intelligence says China's economic support and growing trade have helped Tehran withstand US-led sanctions; oil purchases are not named here.

assertions.quote: Now they become, to some extent, Achilles heels because they can be attacked.

verdicts.note: Iran struck Al Udeid in 2025, and 2026 sources report Gulf bases and hosts hit again.
During the 2026 war Iraqi Shia militias answered Iran's call to attack US bases, causing some damage; the assessment shows bases as targets but says little about attacks on host countries.

assertions.quote: I think he may perceive a window to take the gloves off and do the things that he felt hamstrung from doing

verdicts.note: A forecast made a week before the vote; carrier deployments make it plausible but it had not happened.

assertions.quote: the fact that these Iraqi affiliated groups are hitting Saudi Arabia to me seems to pretty firmly indicate Iranian involvement.

verdicts.note: Reported Houthi and Iraqi militia attacks on Saudi Arabia fit the claim, but how far Iran directs them is disputed.
UCDP records Houthi-linked interstate conflicts with Israel (2025) and with the US and UK over the Red Sea (2024-2025), supporting the Red Sea part; it does not cover Saudi Arabia or 2026.

assertions.quote: we've already seen complaints from PACOM and EUCOM that it's not sustainable
The war in Iran is deeply unpopular with the U.S. public, with just one in three Americans supporting it.

verdicts.note: Polls cited in two 2026 sources show majorities opposed.
